verification.policy: A status of 'verified' means the behavior was checked, not that it looked right while somebody was reading the code. So an entry carries 'verified_on': for each platform, the suites whose tests cover it. An entry may be 'verified' only when every platform listed below appears in that map, because a command that only ever ran on one host is not a claim about the other one; and a suite that is not listed under a platform cannot be cited for it. The notes stay authoritative about what is missing either way - evidence for the parts that are covered does not certify the rest, which is why --require-full fails while any entry is not verified.

linux.how: make -C source/linux all check && make -C source/linux check-live

suites.unit: source/linux/tests/UnitTest.cpp - 663 checks of the parts that need no I/O: permission and mode parsing, masks, path handling, the transfer and synchronization planners, parameter and timestamp expansion, the stored-session file.
suites.script: source/linux/tests/ScriptTest.py - the command line and script semantics against no server: abbreviations, switches, batch modes and exit codes, local listings, help, -log and -xmllog.
suites.live-sftp: source/linux/tests/LiveSftpTest.py against source/linux/tests/TestSftpServer.py - refused opens (wrong password, unexpected host key), operations the server denies, an interrupted download and its resume, a transfer that outlives the connection, and timestamps in both directions.
suites.manual: Hand-run against the same server, kept here because no automated test does it yet: 'chmod -recursive' octal and symbolic over a tree, 'copyid' with an OpenSSH .pub and with a private key, 'put -append', 'get -append', -resumesupport=64 across a partial file, -speed=40, -preservetime=all on a directory, -xmllog= with -parameter. Reproduce with source/linux/build/linuxscp -batch -hostkey='*' -command="open sftp://testuser:testpass@127.0.0.1:12765/ ; ..." after starting the server.

windows.how: cmake -S . -B build -A x64 && cmake --build build --config Release && ctest --test-dir build -C Release

suites.unit: linuxscp-unittest.exe, the same C++ checks, built and run by the MSVC and MinGW jobs.
suites.script: ScriptTest.py against linuxscp.exe - the command line, batch modes, exit codes, local listings and help, which is where a Windows path or separator difference shows.
suites.live-sftp: LiveSftpTest.py against the paramiko server the job starts itself: refused opens, an unexpected host key and a resumed download after the connection died. The POSIX-only cases - Ctrl-C, directory write protection, -preservetime on an upload - skip themselves and say why.

windows.cannot_prove: The native PuTTY SFTP transport does not exist on Windows, so SFTP here means curl; there is no POSIX server for it to see how permissions, symlinks or path semantics behave against one, and no Windows box in this project's CI has a live server to compare against.

!.notes: Runs the command over SSH exec in a one-shot second connection and prints its output, like upstream 'call'. No interactive shell with a pty.

ascii.notes: Sets 'option transfer ascii' like upstream, with arity checks; the conversion is applied by get/put/synchronize and was verified byte-exact against a live server. No per-site transfer presets.

binary.notes: Sets 'option transfer binary' like upstream, with arity checks. No per-site transfer presets.

bye.notes: Basic command implemented; full upstream argument, output and session semantics have not been verified.

call.notes: Rejoins and re-quotes the arguments and runs them over SSH exec in a one-shot second connection (the main SFTP session stays open). No interactive shell with a pty.

cd.notes: With no argument it goes to the home directory captured at connect time and prints the resulting directory, like upstream; 'cd <dir>' also prints. No directory history.

checksum.notes: Server-side check-file-name extension first, then a local sha-256/sha-1/md5/crc32 fallback through the PuTTY core; prints '<hash> <file>' like upstream. Verified live against a server without the extension (fallback path); the server-side path needs a server that implements check-file.

chmod.notes: Octal and symbolic modes ('u+x', 'a=r,go-w', 'u+s', 'X') and -recursive over a directory tree, symbolic links skipped; the mode is checked before the connection so a typo is reported even when offline. Upstream's script command passes an octal string only, so the symbolic forms and the recursion are an extension; verified against a live server that implements SETSTAT. Missing: owner and group changes, and upstream's per-site permission defaults.

close.notes: Single connection only; no indexed session close.

copyid.notes: Reads the session's private key (or the given key file: an OpenSSH public key, an OpenSSH private key or a PuTTY .ppk, foreign formats imported through the bundled PuTTY core) and appends its authorized_keys line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, creating the directory 0700 and the file 0600 and leaving an already installed key alone. Needs an sftp:// or scp:// session; an encrypted key asks for its passphrase in an interactive session and is refused in batch mode. The Windows build says it cannot read key files instead of doing nothing. Verified live for .pub, PEM private and duplicate input; the upstream command takes exactly one argument, ours also accepts none.

cp.notes: Server-side copy-data extension with a streamed fallback through the local host, recursive directory trees, multi-source into an existing directory and confirm-on-overwrite. Verified live via the fallback path; the native path needs a server with the copy-data extension.

dir.notes: Listing whose mask comes from the trailing path component ('ls docs/*.log'), like upstream. Long format is the SFTP longname, not upstream's column formatting.

echo.notes: Plain token output. The line has already been through the upstream expansions - script parameters, %TIMESTAMP% and environment variables - because they are applied before dispatch; text in single quotes is left alone.

exit.notes: Basic command implemented; full upstream argument, output and session semantics have not been verified.

get.notes: Binary/ASCII/automatic transfers with full WinSCP file masks (name, directory and path masks, size/time criteria), -filemask=, option include/exclude, failonnomatch, resume (binary only, rejected with ASCII), -resumesupport=on|off|<KB>, -append (native SFTP only), -speed=<KB/s>, -neweronly/-noneweronly and -preservetime[=all]. Speed, append, resume and the time preservation were verified against a live SFTP server. Missing: transfer presets, -permissions on downloads and upstream's raw transfer settings.

help.notes: Per-command 'help <command> / 'man <command>' with syntax lines and a general listing. Command names, including those in help, may be given as an unambiguous abbreviation.

keepuptodate.notes: Takes no direction word, like upstream, and accepts -delete, -filemask=, -transfer=, -interval=, -count= and -continue (keeps watching after a failed pass). Still a scripted poll loop, not the upstream background watcher: no file-system event source and no 'stop' command.

lcd.notes: Basic command implemented; full upstream argument, output and session semantics have not been verified.

lls.notes: Local directories and simple wildcard masks; names-only output, not upstream formatting.

ln.notes: SFTP SYMLINK with the upstream argument order (target, link), verified live. Fails explicitly on protocols without symlinks.

lpwd.notes: Basic command implemented; full upstream argument, output and session semantics have not been verified.

ls.notes: Listing whose mask comes from the trailing path component ('ls docs/*.log'), like upstream. Long format is the SFTP longname, not upstream's column formatting.

man.notes: Same as 'help': per-command syntax and a general listing, with unambiguous abbreviations accepted.

mget.notes: Same implementation as 'get', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Missing: transfer presets.

mkdir.notes: Basic command implemented; full upstream argument, output and session semantics have not been verified.

mput.notes: Same implementation as 'put', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Missing: transfer presets.

mv.notes: Multi-source with an existing-directory target, rename in place and confirm-on-overwrite, like upstream.

open.notes: URL sessions and stored-session names; an unknown host key is refused and reported on a HOSTKEY line so it can be pinned. No raw settings, SSH tunnels, session folders or session selection UI in the console client.

option.notes: echo, batch (on/off/abort/continue), confirm, resume, transfer (binary/ascii/automatic), include/exclude (one mask, setting either clears the other, 'clear' resets), synchdelete, failonnomatch, reconnecttime (seconds or off, with automatic reconnect), editor, editmaxsize, and a listing when called with no name. Option and value names may be abbreviated when the abbreviation is unambiguous; masks, programs and numbers are never abbreviated. Missing: transfer presets and per-site persistence of script options.

put.notes: Binary/ASCII/automatic transfers with WinSCP file masks, -filemask=, option include/exclude, failonnomatch, -permissions=/-nopermissions, and the -resume, -append, -speed=, -resumesupport=, -neweronly/-noneweronly and -preservetime[=all] switches of 'get' (append and resume are mutually exclusive and need the native SFTP transport). Verified against a live server. Missing: transfer presets and upstream's raw transfer settings.

pwd.notes: Basic command implemented; full upstream argument, output and session semantics have not been verified.

recv.notes: Same implementation as 'get', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Missing: transfer presets.

rename.notes: One source and one destination only.

rm.notes: Multiple files, masks and -onlyfile (directories are skipped with a status), no-match reporting gated by option failonnomatch, like upstream. No recursive delete, matching upstream.

rmdir.notes: Multiple directories in one command, continuing past failures; only empty directories, like upstream.

send.notes: Same implementation as 'put', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Missing: transfer presets.

session.notes: Lists the stored sessions from sessions.ini. The non-upstream helpers savesession and rmsession create and remove them, and 'open <name>' resolves a stored session, but there is no folder tree, no raw settings and no password encryption.

stat.notes: Basic command implemented; full upstream argument, output and session semantics have not been verified.

symlink.notes: Alias of 'ln': SFTP SYMLINK with the upstream argument order (target, link). Fails explicitly on protocols without symlinks.

synchronize.notes: Planner with direction, -criteria=, -filemask=, -delete/-nodelete (default from option synchdelete), -mirror (rejects 'both', resolves any difference toward the source), -transfer=binary|ascii|automatic, -preview, -nonrecursive, -interval=, -count=; 'both' keeps a state record. Verified live. Missing: watch/background mode and upstream's conflict resolution UI.

features.name: SFTP
features.notes: Native PuTTY transport on POSIX; Windows uses curl. SYMLINK, copy-data (with a streamed fallback) and check-file-name (with a local hash fallback) are implemented and were verified against a live in-process SFTP server; unknown extensions still fail explicitly rather than being ignored.

features.name: SCP
features.notes: Delegated to curl, whose SCP support depends on its build; no WinSCP shell-based directory and command engine.

features.name: FTP/FTPS
features.notes: curl transport and listing parser; no full upstream MLSD, TLS configuration, active/passive and server compatibility validation.

features.name: WebDAV
features.notes: Generic HTTP listing parsing, not DAV PROPFIND XML; incomplete directory/property semantics.

features.name: Amazon S3
features.notes: s3 URLs currently become HTTPS; no AWS SigV4 signing, credentials/region configuration or S3 bucket/object listing implementation.

features.name: Transfers
features.notes: Binary and ASCII/automatic transfers with full WinSCP file masks (name, directory and path masks plus size/time criteria), include/exclude options, failonnomatch, resume with a -resumesupport= threshold (binary only), -append to add to an existing file, -speed= bandwidth limiting (pacing in the native engine, curl --limit-rate elsewhere), -preservetime with -preservetime=all for directories, and reconnecttime with automatic reconnect; ASCII conversion, speed, append, resume and times were verified byte-exact or by timing against a live server. Missing: transfer presets, the .filepart temporary-name policy and per-file progress reporting on the curl paths.

features.name: Synchronization
features.notes: Planner with direction, -criteria=time|size|either|none, -filemask=, -delete/-nodelete (option synchdelete as the default), -mirror (any difference resolves toward the source; rejected with 'both'), -transfer=binary|ascii|automatic applied to planned transfers, -preview, -nonrecursive, -interval=, -count= and keepuptodate -continue; 'both' keeps a state record to tell changes from conflicts. Verified live. Missing: watch/background mode and upstream's conflict resolution UI.

features.name: Sessions/configuration
features.notes: sessions.ini site manager shared by the console and the graphical client: session, savesession, rmsession, 'open <name>', export/import and last-used tracking. Missing: folder tree, raw settings, encrypted passwords and the full upstream configuration model.

features.name: Security/authentication
features.notes: POSIX password/key/agent and host-key policy exist; an unknown or changed key is refused and reported instead of being accepted. GSSAPI is compiled out; proxy/tunnel configuration and curl fingerprint equivalence are incomplete. The graphical interface now verifies by default, pins on request and stores a pin rather than a wildcard, and its API is bound to loopback behind a per-run token with a Host check; there is still no user account or encrypted credential store.

features.name: GUI
features.notes: Browser Commander with one persistent session per tab, dual panes, a transfer queue with progress/pause/cancel/retry, synchronization preview, remote search, a remote editor, the site manager and host-key pinning, driven by a loopback HTTP API behind a per-run token (Host-checked) over -server; the client has a jsdom regression test. Still not upstream Commander/Explorer: no drag and drop, custom commands, synchronized browsing or localization.

features.name: Editing/search
features.notes: 'edit' downloads, runs the configured editor and uploads on change, with a size limit and a refusal when the remote file changed meanwhile; remote search matches name masks recursively. Missing: save/upload monitoring of local edits, full-text search, encoding handling and the custom command system.

features.name: Automation
features.notes: Console scripting with WinSCP switches, unambiguous command and option abbreviations, script parameters (%1%..%9% via -parameter), %TIMESTAMP% with relative offsets and formats, %NAME% environment expansion, and an XML action log (-xmllog=) recording every command, result, message and transfer with passwords masked. Missing: the WinSCP .NET assembly and PowerShell APIs, and equivalence with upstream's log format, which our log mirrors in structure but does not copy; the expansions are not applied to -server input, where the graphical client quotes literal paths.

features.name: Desktop integration
features.notes: Debian launcher/icons and terminal launch exist; no full upstream drag/drop, shell integration or extension system.

features.name: Localization/accessibility
features.notes: No equivalent upstream translation catalog and desktop accessibility verification.

features.name: Packaging/platforms
features.notes: Make/CMake and Debian/Windows builds exist; Windows curl may lack SSH protocols. Native builds do not establish functional parity.

linuxscp_additions.name: edit
linuxscp_additions.notes: Downloads the remote file, runs $LINUXSCP_EDITOR/$EDITOR or option editor, and uploads it back when it changed, refusing files over option editmaxsize and refusing to overwrite a file modified since the download. No local-side edit, no editor fallback chain or encoding handling beyond the installed editor. Upstream's script interpreter has no 'edit' command at the pinned commit, so this is a LinuxSCP command rather than parity work.

linuxscp_additions.name: savesession / rmsession
linuxscp_additions.notes: Store and forget a named site in sessions.ini, which 'open <name>' and the graphical site manager then resolve. Upstream has no such script commands; it edits the configuration through its GUI and the .NET assembly.

linuxscp_additions.name: sessions
linuxscp_additions.notes: Plural alias of 'session' with no argument, listing the stored sites. Not an upstream command name.

linuxscp_additions.name: show
linuxscp_additions.notes: Recognised only to report that it is unsupported: the connection runs the SFTP subsystem, so there is no shell state to show. Not an upstream script command either.

linuxscp_additions.name: del, md, sync, quit, end
linuxscp_additions.notes: Extra aliases accepted for convenience (rm, mkdir, synchronize, exit, exit). Upstream registers 'dir' but not these, so they are not counted as upstream coverage.
